cb7a5731c8c9eaa295a1a99550008cae3f5805e3: Ladis's 186 km of pistes make for a fine offer for all profiles: big enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. The 38 lifts let you link runs without long queues. Ladis has kept an authentic mountain village identity, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for clean air, unspoilt landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some big ski areas. With a summit at 2828 m and a village at 1190 m, Ladis's snow reliability is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. The budget for a stay in Ladis is clearly high: 78€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but be aware of it before you set off. In short: Ladis lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
